meta.summary: A dark, restrained B2B landing experience where motion does two jobs: it eases content in with long, low-travel expo-out fades, and it demonstrates the product through a scripted, looping illustration that shows cause and effect step by step. Interactive chrome is deliberately quiet: hovers swap colour or border on a gently damped spring, nothing lifts or scales, and every scroll reveal fires once and stays put. Choreography is container-driven: one trigger per section, children staggered by index, numbers counting up only after their frame has grown in. The UX is a single long page with a persistent booking call to action and anchor navigation, with conversion handed off to external tools.
meta.product_type: marketing site (single-page B2B SaaS landing page)

principles.description: Reveals travel 4 to 24px at most and rely on long expo-out tails (0.8 to 2s) so content appears to settle rather than arrive.
principles.how_to_apply: Use ease-out-expo with reveal offsets of 4px for display text, 16px for dense grids and 24px for cards. Never exceed 24px of vertical travel on a scroll reveal.

principles.description: The biggest motion budget goes into a scripted product illustration that shows an input being parsed, items extracted, carried to their destination and confirmed.
principles.how_to_apply: Build explanatory animations as timelines of discrete states with a clear source, travel and confirmation beat, then hold the end state for about 3.2s before looping.

principles.description: Buttons and links respond with colour, border or fill changes only, on a soft spring (0.4s, bounce 0.2) or a 200ms tween.
principles.how_to_apply: No hover lift, scale or shadow growth on buttons. The only transform on hover is a single 360 degree icon rotation on media buttons.

principles.description: Each section observes its container once and staggers children by index, so a whole block reads as one gesture.
principles.how_to_apply: Attach a single IntersectionObserver (threshold 0.15, or 0.3 for stat blocks) to the section wrapper and delay children by index times 90ms.

principles.principle: Reveal once, then get out of the way
principles.description: Scroll reveals never replay or reverse, so scrolling back up is calm. The single exception is a decorative separator that slides in and out.
principles.how_to_apply: Disconnect observers after the first intersection. Reserve repeatable enter and exit for purely decorative elements.

principles.principle: Conversion is always one tap away
principles.description: The primary booking action sits in the fixed header and repeats after most major sections, usually paired with a secondary sign-in action.
principles.how_to_apply: Keep a compact primary CTA in the persistent nav and repeat a full-size primary plus secondary pair at the hero and final section, with single full-width CTA bands between.

principles.principle: Load settles fast and never blocks reading
principles.description: The hero sequence finishes in about 2.3s and starts from opacity 0.001 before hydration, so text is readable almost immediately.
principles.how_to_apply: Start hero motion within 30 to 400ms of first paint, use opacity-first reveals, and keep secondary actions on a short 400ms fade that lands last.

springs.usage: Default button hover, mobile menu open and close, hamburger-to-cross morph, widest-breakpoint pop-in. Exact source form is a duration-based spring { duration: 0.4s, bounce: 0.2 }; the stiffness and damping here are an approximate conversion, so prefer the duration and bounce form in Framer Motion.

distances.reveal_offset: 24px for cards, 16px for dense grids, 4px for display characters, 3 to 4px for demo micro-entrances
distances.hover_lift: 0px (no lift; hover is colour, border or fill only)
distances.slide_distance: 300px (decorative separator slides in from the left)

tokens.entrance_exit_ratio: 1:1 wherever an exit exists (hover out mirrors hover in; the separator slides out on the same 1s curve). Scroll reveals are one-shot with no exit.

patterns.name: hero-heading-char-rise
patterns.interruptible: Not re-triggerable; state flips once on mount.
patterns.applies_to: Primary display heading on landing templates, including an inline logo glyph treated as one character.
patterns.responsive_differences: Same timing at all breakpoints; only size changes.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Source has no reduced-motion branch here (only a 30ms mount timer). Recommended: render final state with no transition.
patterns.ux_purpose: Signals craft and draws the eye to the value proposition first without delaying legibility, because travel is only 4px and opacity leads.

patterns.name: hero-sequenced-fade
patterns.applies_to: Hero subline (400ms delay, 1200ms), hero action group (600ms delay, 1200ms), and one action inside the group on a short late fade (1000ms delay, 400ms).
patterns.responsive_differences: Identical values across all four breakpoints.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Framer appear effects can be configured to respect reduced motion but this could not be verified live. Recommended: show immediately.
patterns.ux_purpose: Establishes reading order: headline, then supporting line, then actions, so the call to action lands once the promise is understood.

patterns.name: card-grid-rise
patterns.exit_behaviour: None; observer disconnects after first reveal.
patterns.interruptible: No. Scrolling away mid-reveal lets the transition finish.
patterns.applies_to: Numbered step grids (16px offset, 1500ms), two-column feature cards (24px, 1000ms), role or use-case lists (24px, 1000ms). Component default is 24px and 800ms.
patterns.responsive_differences: Column count comes from container width (1 column under 600px, 2 under 960px, 4 above), so stagger order follows DOM order and reads top to bottom on phones.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: The grid component short-circuits the reveal through a runtime hook (likely reduced-motion or static render, not verified). Recommended: render shown state.
patterns.ux_purpose: Groups a section into one readable gesture and walks the eye across items in reading order.

patterns.name: lottie-in-view-play

trigger.start: 15% visible (feature cards) or on load with loop (step grid)

patterns.exit_behaviour: Holds last frame (play-once cards) or keeps looping (step grid illustrations).
patterns.interruptible: Plays once per page view; not restarted by re-entry.
patterns.applies_to: Illustration slot inside numbered feature cards and step cards.
patterns.responsive_differences: Illustration width drops to 90% on narrow cards.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Not handled in source. Recommended: jump to final frame.
patterns.ux_purpose: Each card illustrates its idea at the moment it is read; the delay equals the card stagger so the illustration starts as its card finishes arriving.

patterns.name: stat-block-grow-count
patterns.applies_to: Headline metric blocks. Grow 600ms (1000ms at one breakpoint); corner markers fade over 300ms after 60% of grow; label fades over 400ms after 50% of grow; number counts over 1200ms with ease-out-cubic after a 300ms hold.
patterns.responsive_differences: Grow duration lengthens to 1000ms at the 1440px-and-up layout where the block is largest.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Not handled in source. Recommended: show final value and full-size block.
patterns.ux_purpose: Makes a single proof point feel earned: the frame claims space first, then the number climbs, which holds attention for about 1.5s on the key metric.

patterns.name: scramble-type-on

properties.content: random glyphs of the same length

patterns.applies_to: Monospaced captions under stat blocks, right aligned, resolving from the right edge.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Not handled in source. Recommended: show final text.

patterns.name: separator-slide
patterns.exit_behaviour: Slides back to -300px on the same 1s curve when it leaves the viewport; replays on re-entry. One breakpoint override sets it to play once.
patterns.interruptible: Yes; reverses from its current position.
patterns.applies_to: Decorative dashed or patterned divider between sections (element is twice the viewport width so the offset never exposes an edge).
patterns.responsive_differences: Appear effect disabled at the phone breakpoint; once-only at the widest breakpoint.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Not handled in source. Recommended: static divider.

patterns.name: spring-pop-in
patterns.applies_to: A single emphasis card in the metrics section, widest breakpoint only.
patterns.responsive_differences: Only defined at 1440px and up; other breakpoints render it statically.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: static.
patterns.ux_purpose: One deliberate moment of physicality to spotlight a metric; rarity is what makes it work.

patterns.name: button-hover-spring-fill
patterns.exit_behaviour: Returns to rest on the same spring (1:1).
patterns.interruptible: Yes; spring retargets from current value.
patterns.applies_to: Full-size primary (fill deepens, border removed), secondary and hollow buttons (border and label shift to {color.brand}).
patterns.responsive_differences: Hover only on pointer devices; touch gets no pressed state.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Colour change can stay; it is not motion.
patterns.ux_purpose: Confirms the element is actionable with a calm, non-bouncy acknowledgement that fits the technical tone.

patterns.name: compact-button-hover
patterns.applies_to: Header outline CTA (fills on hover), small brand buttons, plain-text header link. One small secondary variant changes instantly (0ms).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Unchanged (colour only).
patterns.ux_purpose: Snappier feedback where the target is small and frequently used, so the header feels responsive.

patterns.name: icon-button-spin

patterns.applies_to: Extracted typed tags moving from the source panel to their target row.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Items shown at destination only (source).

patterns.name: demo-pop-confirm
patterns.exit_behaviour: None; the new value stays. Optional colour tint settles from {color.accent} to resting over 1800ms.
patterns.applies_to: Counters, badges, date labels and risk chips inside the demo when they update.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Animation none (source).
patterns.ux_purpose: Confirms that the change landed; the 8% overshoot is the only bounce in the system and is confined to tiny elements.

patterns.name: demo-row-flash

trigger.start: row receives an update or mention

patterns.exit_behaviour: Fades out and stays hidden (fill forwards). A thin accent bar rises in (300ms, 4px) on mentioned rows and remains.
patterns.applies_to: Table or timeline rows in the demo.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Overlay hidden (source).
patterns.ux_purpose: Draws the eye to where the change happened without a persistent highlight.

patterns.name: demo-status-pulse
patterns.applies_to: Live or connected status dots in the demo (a 9px accent variant marks the active agent).
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: static dot.
patterns.ux_purpose: Signals that the system is live and working in the background.

patterns.name: demo-listening-indicators
patterns.applies_to: Thinking dots, audio level bars (scaleY 0.35 to 1), caret blink and spinner inside the demo input.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Recommended: static icons.
patterns.ux_purpose: Reduces perceived wait inside the simulated interaction and makes the state legible at a glance.

patterns.name: demo-marker-shift
patterns.exit_behaviour: Snaps back with no transition at loop reset.
patterns.applies_to: Date or milestone markers on a timeline that move when a plan changes.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Transition none (source).
patterns.ux_purpose: Shows consequence: a schedule change visibly moves the dependent marker.

patterns.name: badge-shine-sweep
patterns.interruptible: Hover shortens the loop to 1300ms; because the duration changes mid-run the sweep jumps position (source behaviour).
patterns.applies_to: Small third-party badges in the footer area.
patterns.reduced_motion_fallback: Not handled in source. Recommended: hide the sweep.

choreography_rules: Hero: heading characters start 30ms after mount (30ms stagger, 2s each); subline fades at 400ms; the action group fades at 600ms; the second action lands last at 1000ms with a short 400ms fade. Everything settles by about 2.3s.
Load-time elements start from opacity 0.001, not 0, and are animated by a pre-hydration script so first paint is never blank.
One IntersectionObserver per section container; children stagger by DOM index at 90ms, so grids read left to right, then top to bottom.
Illustrations inside cards start after their card’s stagger slot (index x stagger, minimum 120ms), never before their card is visible.
Metric blocks: frame grows first (600ms), label fades at 50% of grow, corner markers at 60%, the number starts counting only after a 300ms hold and runs 1200ms.

Explainer timelines follow source, then travel, then confirm: highlight the input (60ms per word), spawn the item at the source (300ms), travel to destination (800ms, 80ms stagger between items), confirm with a flash (1400ms) and pop (450ms), then hold 3200ms before looping.
Only one continuously looping illustration per viewport; ambient loops elsewhere are limited to tiny status dots and badge shine.
Hover feedback never moves layout: colour, border and fill only; the only hover transform is a 360 degree icon spin on media buttons.
Scroll reveals are one-shot; the only repeatable enter and exit is a decorative separator.
Nothing is scroll-scrubbed, pinned or parallaxed.

reduced_motion.strategy: Only the scripted product demo explicitly honours prefers-reduced-motion (jumps to the final state, animations none). The site runtime disables view-transition animations under reduced motion. The grid reveal is gated by a runtime hook that could not be confirmed as reduced-motion. Hero character rise, stat grow and count, type-on text, separator slide, badge shine and the mobile ticker have no reduced-motion handling in code. Replicas should render final states for all of these.

motion_system.performance_notes: Mostly transform and opacity, with will-change on hero characters. Exceptions: the demo animates left (timeline markers), box-shadow (status pulses), filter blur (word stream) and background-color (highlight sweep), which are paint-heavy but confined to small elements. The demo timeline keeps running when scrolled off screen (running CSS animations were observed while the footer was in view), so replicas should pause it with an IntersectionObserver. Lottie uses the SVG renderer at medium quality and the player script is included twice. Fixed-size demo canvases are scaled with a CSS transform from a ResizeObserver, avoiding reflow.

information_architecture.depth: 1 click to book a demo or sign in from anywhere (fixed header); 1 click to any in-page section via anchors; resources open in a new tab.

page_templates.name: landing
page_templates.purpose: Explain the product and convert to a booked demo or sign-in
section_order: fixed header with inline anchor links and compact primary CTA
hero: display heading, subline, primary plus secondary action pair
looping product illustration in a framed panel
how-it-works heading plus four-step numbered grid with illustrations
systems section: two-column numbered feature cards with play-once illustrations, secondary hollow CTA
metrics section: grow-and-count stat blocks with type-on captions
role or use-case list with oversized side callout and full-width CTA band
final CTA with primary plus secondary pair

navigation.primary: Fixed top bar, always visible, solid background, no hide-on-scroll, no condensing and no style change on scroll (checked at several scroll depths on desktop). Left: logo link home. Centre: in-page anchor links separated by small dividers. Right: plain-text sign-in and an outline compact primary CTA.
navigation.mobile: Below 810px the inline links collapse into a two-bar toggle. Tapping expands the header in place (height grows on spring-soft) to show large stacked anchor links, a smaller secondary link and a full-width primary CTA; the bars rotate +/-45 degrees into a cross. No scrim, no body scroll lock, no Escape handling, and the panel stays open after tapping an anchor link (observed).
navigation.secondary: Repeated in-content CTAs, footer navigation, and an external resources link that opens in a new tab.
navigation.wayfinding: None: no active-section highlighting, no scroll progress, no section indicators. Numbered labels (01/, 02/ ...) give sequence within sections.

forms.error_presentation: Not applicable: the page has no forms; all data capture happens on external pages.

feedback_and_states.perceived_performance: Load-appear effects are driven by an inline pre-hydration animator starting from opacity 0.001, so the hero is animating before the app hydrates. Illustrations show a flat placeholder or poster until loaded. The explainer starts from a calm idle state rather than a spinner.
feedback_and_states.errors: Not applicable on page; illustration load failures only log to console.
feedback_and_states.success: Within the explainer, successful actions are confirmed by row flashes, overshoot pops and colour settles.

attention_and_hierarchy.cta_strategy: Primary booking CTA in the fixed header plus repeated in-content instances (hero pair, mid-page hollow, full-width band, final pair). Secondary is always sign-in. Primary is filled; secondary and hollow are outlined.
attention_and_hierarchy.attention_direction: Load motion walks headline, subline, actions in order. The explainer then pulls focus with cause-and-effect beats. Scroll sections reveal as units with left-to-right stagger. Numbers and illustrations only animate after their frame arrives, so the eye lands on the frame first.
attention_and_hierarchy.progressive_disclosure: Minimal. Only the phone menu hides content. Everything else is visible on scroll; no accordions, tabs or modals.

breakpoint_behaviour.changes: Widest layout; stat blocks larger with 1000ms grow; spring pop-in active on one metric card; separator plays once.
Same interaction model as widest; spacing and sizes step down.
Inline nav retained (tablet header variant); grids drop to two columns by container width. Not visually tested.
Menu toggle replaces inline links; hero actions stack full width; logo row becomes a ticker; feature cards go single column; card numbers move to the top-right; separator appear effect disabled.

responsive_behaviour.touch_adaptations: Hover affordances simply disappear on touch (no pressed states). Large stacked menu links (about 38px tall) and full-width CTAs. No gestures (ticker not draggable, no swipe).

accessibility.focus_visibility: Browser default outline on all nav and CTA links; no custom focus-visible styling. Several badge links remove the outline entirely.
accessibility.semantics: No header, nav, main or footer landmarks. Heading levels skip (an h3 precedes the first h2; h5 used late). Mobile menu links are wrapped in heading elements. All actions are anchors (correct for navigation). The explainer is a single role img with a descriptive label. html lang is set; all images carry alt attributes.
accessibility.screen_reader_notes: Hero heading splits into per-character spans with no aria-label on the heading, so some screen readers may read it letter by letter. Animated counters expose intermediate values. Ticker duplicates are not hidden. Not tested with a real screen reader.
issues_found: Menu toggle is a focusable div with no role, accessible name or aria-expanded
Mobile menu: no Escape, no outside-tap close, does not close after anchor navigation, no focus management
Several zero-size links in the badge area stay in the tab order, creating invisible focus stops
Badge links suppress the focus outline
Desktop nav text links are about 19px tall, below the 24px WCAG 2.2 minimum target size
Autoplaying looping explainer has no pause control
Most scroll and text animations ignore prefers-reduced-motion
Anchor navigation does not move focus to the target section
External links opening a new tab give no warning

do: Use ease-out-expo for every scroll reveal with 16 to 24px travel and 0.8 to 1.5s duration
Trigger each section once from its container and stagger children by index at 90ms
Start load-time elements at opacity 0.001 and finish the hero sequence within about 2.3s
Keep button hovers to colour, border or fill on spring-soft (0.4s, bounce 0.2) or 200ms ease-soft for compact controls
Grow metric frames before counting, and count with ease-out-cubic after a 300ms hold using tabular figures
Build explainers as discrete-state timelines: highlight source, spawn item, travel with ease-travel, confirm with flash and pop, hold 3.2s, loop
Delay card illustrations until their card stagger slot has passed
Keep the compact primary CTA in the fixed header at every breakpoint
Render final states under prefers-reduced-motion for every pattern (the source only does this for the explainer)
Pause off-screen loops with an IntersectionObserver
dont: Do not add hover lift, scale or shadow growth to buttons or cards
Do not use bouncy springs outside tiny confirmation pops (the only overshoot is 8% on small badges)
Do not replay scroll reveals on scroll-up or add direction-aware exits
Do not add parallax, pinning or scroll-scrubbed sequences; the system has none
Do not travel more than 24px on reveals or animate large blocks from off-screen
Do not hide or condense the header on scroll
Do not animate layout properties such as left, width or height for anything larger than a small marker; use transform
Do not rely on hover-only affordances for anything essential on touch
Do not copy the source mobile-menu gaps (div toggle, no Escape, stays open after navigation)

implementation.target_stack: React 18 + Framer Motion (motion/react) + Tailwind CSS, with plain CSS transitions for IntersectionObserver reveals. This mirrors the source, which mixes Framer Motion variants with hand-written CSS transitions in custom React components. The prompt left the target stack unspecified, so this choice is based on the evidence.
recommended_libraries: motion (Framer Motion) for hover springs, variants, whileInView and height-auto menu animation
No smooth-scroll library: the source uses native scrolling plus a short JS anchor tween

ai_replication_prompt: Build every new screen with the Calm Technical Showcase Motion system. Import the motion tokens (CSS variables and the DUR, EASE, SPRING, STAGGER, DIST constants) and the presets module, and never invent new curves. Scroll content uses card-grid-rise: one IntersectionObserver per section container (threshold 0.15), children fade from opacity 0 and 16 to 24px below with ease-out-expo over 1 to 1.5s, staggered by index at stagger_ms.base (90ms), revealed once and never reversed. The hero uses hero-heading-char-rise (characters rise 4px behind an overflow mask, 2s ease-out-expo, 30ms stagger, starting 30ms after mount) followed by hero-sequenced-fade (subline at 400ms, action group at 600ms, both 1200ms ease-soft, final action at 1000ms over 400ms), all starting from opacity 0.001. Metrics use stat-block-grow-count: the frame scales from its bottom-left corner over 600ms, label and corner markers fade at 50 and 60% of the grow, then the number counts up for 1200ms with ease-out-cubic after a 300ms hold. Supporting captions use scramble-type-on resolving from the right in about 744ms. Illustrations follow lottie-in-view-play and start only after their card stagger slot. Buttons follow button-hover-spring-fill: colour, border or fill changes on spring-soft (duration 0.4, bounce 0.2); compact header controls use compact-button-hover at 200ms ease-soft; links use text-link-colour. No lifts, scales, shadows, parallax, pinning or scrubbing anywhere. The only hover transform is icon-button-spin on media buttons. Explainer panels are scripted timelines (product-demo-scripted-loop): highlight source words (demo-highlight-sweep, 60ms per word), spawn items at the source (300ms ease-snap), move them to their destination (demo-chip-travel, 800ms ease-travel, 80ms apart), confirm with demo-row-flash and demo-pop-confirm (450ms, 8% overshoot), hold the end state 3200ms, then loop. Pause explainers off screen. Keep a fixed, always-visible header with inline anchor links (anchor-smooth-scroll, about 850ms ease-in-out) and a compact primary CTA; below 810px use mobile-menu-expand, where the header grows in place on spring-soft and the two bars rotate into a cross. Use a real button with aria-expanded, close on Escape and on link tap. Repeat the primary booking CTA after most sections and pair it with an outline secondary in the hero and final section. Under prefers-reduced-motion, render every final state instantly.

gaps.area: Timing under a hidden browser pane
gaps.issue: The inspection browser pane was hidden for part of the session, which throttles requestAnimationFrame. The anchor-scroll duration (about 850ms) and ticker motion were observed under these conditions; code-read values are unaffected.
gaps.suggested_approach: Re-measure anchor scroll and ticker speed in a visible browser with a performance trace.

gaps.issue: prefers-reduced-motion could not be emulated in the test browser. Reduced-motion support is inferred from code only.
gaps.suggested_approach: Toggle reduced motion in DevTools rendering settings and re-check hero, grid, stat and ticker behaviour.

gaps.issue: The 810 to 1199px layout was not visually tested (768px falls in the phone breakpoint). Behaviour is taken from breakpoint definitions and variant names.
gaps.suggested_approach: Test at 1024px for header variant, grid columns and reveal behaviour.

gaps.issue: No pressed variants were found; Enter or Space activation of the div-based menu toggle was not verified.
gaps.suggested_approach: Test keyboard activation of the toggle and record any active-state styling in a live session.

gaps.issue: The grid reveal is skipped by a runtime hook imported from the site builder; whether it is reduced-motion, static render or editor detection was not confirmed.
gaps.suggested_approach: Emulate reduced motion and compare initial grid state.

gaps.issue: The source defines springs as duration 0.4s and bounce 0.2. The stiffness 470 and damping 35 values are an approximate conversion, not code.
gaps.suggested_approach: Use the duration and bounce form directly in Framer Motion; convert with the library if a physics form is required.

gaps.issue: Motion inside the Lottie illustration files was not decomposed.
gaps.suggested_approach: Open the JSON files in a Lottie viewer to extract their internal timing if exact parity is needed.

gaps.issue: Only the home page was inspected. Resources, sign-in and the external scheduler were not analysed, and no page transitions were exercised.
gaps.suggested_approach: Run the same sweep on secondary templates and any in-app pages.

gaps.issue: Assistive-technology notes are based on DOM inspection, not a real screen reader session.
gaps.suggested_approach: Test with NVDA or VoiceOver, focusing on the split hero heading, counters and ticker duplicates.

gaps.issue: The late 1000ms/400ms appear effect is attached to one button inside the hero action group; which of the two buttons it is was inferred from width and nesting rather than confirmed.
gaps.suggested_approach: Record the hero load at high frame rate to confirm which action lands last.

durations_ms.lottie_native: per file (speed 1x; one looping file at 0.5x)

extensions.appear_optimisation: Load effects are serialised as JSON per breakpoint and started by an inline animator before hydration, beginning at opacity 0.001. Replicas in React can approximate this with SSR-rendered initial styles plus CSS transitions triggered on first paint.

confidence_split.ux: medium (interactive sweep limited by hidden pane and no reduced-motion emulation)

extensions.inspection_notes: Values tagged code were read from inline configuration, stylesheets and page component chunks at runtime. Values tagged observed come from live interaction in an emulated 1440, 768 and 375px viewport. No recordings or screenshots were supplied.
